catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class turns a microscope LED on and off: cap.imaging.illumination.v1 requires an intensity in percent and a channel, while DNX64.SetLEDState takes only an on/off state (dnx64.py:388-399). The package uses an x-cap id with an inline boolean schema.
catalogue_requests.summary: Turn the Dino-Lite LED on or off (SetLEDState 0/1).

catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class sets an FLC (flexible light control) level. cap.imaging.illumination.v1 is an intensity/channel write, not this device-specific level, and the DNX64 method has a documented 1 to 6 range (dnx64.py:384). The package uses an x-cap id with an inline integer schema and a sourced limit.
catalogue_requests.summary: Set the Dino-Lite FLC level (SetFLCLevel, 1 to 6).

catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class switches a microscope's illumination off with no input: cap.imaging.illumination.v1 requires a channel and an intensity. This is also the package's safe-state action, so it takes no input and reports led_on.
catalogue_requests.summary: Turn the Dino-Lite LED off (SetLEDState 0), the safe state.

notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed: authored_by is the model, reviewed_by is null, and no human review or hardware run is claimed. The hardware path (native.py and the proprietary Windows DNX64.dll) was never imported or run; it needs the clone root on PYTHONPATH and the vendor SDK installed separately. The driver is R1 because it switches the microscope LED (MHS-004 section 2.1 lists LED illumination under R1); the loader refuses the hardware backend of an unreviewed model-written package only at R2 and R3, so this R1 package does not claim that protection.

NOT COVERED: the live image frames. DNX64 has no frame acquisition method (dnx64.py:8-39); the app reads 2592 x 1944 frames with cv2.VideoCapture (app.py:31-34), which is outside the upstream control class, and the standard has no frame-array transport here, so no image capability is bound and no pixel array is returned. Also not covered: axial illumination (SetAXILevel, removed from the app on purpose, README.MD:167), MicroTouch, EDOF lens movement, the video property API, WiFi image/video resolution, and EFLC (marked 'Not Working', dnx64.py:30).

Limits: ae_target 16 to 20 (dnx64.py:319) and FLC level 1 to 6 (dnx64.py:384) are sourced. exposure_value is Limit.operator_required because no line of the clone states a device exposure range; the app's 1 to 1000 spin box (app.py:132-134) is a UI choice, and site-limits.example.json is only an example overlay. The FLC level is deliberately narrowed to the method's documented 1 to 6 even though the app's spin box also offers 0 (app.py:137-139).

Safety limitation: the SetLEDState docstring says it is controllable only while the camera preview is established (dnx64.py:388-391); the driver does not own the OpenCV preview, so on hardware the LED-off safe state and the e-stop depend on a preview being established by the application.

Licence: the clone has no LICENSE file; README.MD:221 links the MIT text, so the lock pins the card's NOASSERTION/unknown. The lock keeps the card's install block and adds notes: the vendor SDK is a separate licence-gated Windows download (README.MD:115-120). The gate reported no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings and the clone was unmodified. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package; gate.digest is the digest line the check printed.
